newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - September 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - September 6.

text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Friday's Sri Lankan newspapers.
Government and main opposition United National Party must work together to solve the country's ethnic crisis, Justice Minister G. L. Peiris says.
Sri Lanka felicitates visiting cricket teams from Australia, India and Zimbabwe.
The main opposition United National Party celebrates 50 years.
Tamil rebels agree to ceasefire during polio immunisation campaign.
Tamil rebels smuggled bombs and rocket-propelled grenades in bags of onions, rebel suspect in custody says.
Talks with Tamil Tigers only after destroying them militarily, Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte tells parliament.
Heavy rains expected over the island in coming days, Meteorology Department says.
Government examining pros and cons of banning Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam, but still undecided on issue, President Chandrika Kumaratunga tells Indian newspaper.
Motion to extend the emergency for another month passed in parliament.
